# Design: Specify behaviors that shipped without a spec

## Context

The four behaviors are implemented and, for three of them, tested. What
the code does today, which the deltas describe:

| Behavior | Code | Test |
|---|---|---|
| CRLF ADR parsed like LF | `codev-core/src/decisions/parser.rs` (`extract_frontmatter`) | `a_crlf_adr_is_parsed_like_an_lf_one` |
| Seal hashes the raw body, CRLF included | `codev-core/src/decisions/seal.rs` (`body_slice`, `body_hash`) | `hash_with_crlf_is_supported` |
| Status rewrite keeps CRLF and the body bytes | `codev-engine/src/decisions_actions.rs` (`rewrite_frontmatter_status`) | `rewriting_the_status_keeps_a_crlf_body_byte_for_byte` |
| Warning callouts | `codev-cli/src/docs.rs` (`mark_warning_callouts`), `codev-cli/assets/docs.css` (`blockquote.warning`) | `warning_callouts_get_their_own_class` |
| Silent exit on a closed pipe | `codev-cli/src/main.rs`, `Command::Docs` with `--print` | none found |
| Forward slashes in `init --inherit` paths | `codev-cli/src/commands.rs` (`resolve_inherits`, `portable`) | `init_writes_inherits_and_pins_git_sources`, run on the Windows CI job |

The constraint is that this change modifies no code (proposal, What
Changes). Specs are written against the code; where the code has a limit,
the spec states the limit rather than an ideal.

## Goals / Non-Goals

Goals: each behavior has a requirement with scenarios, so that removing
it breaks a spec; the specs stay observable (no function names).

Non-Goals: changing any behavior, normalizing seals, covering the
relative local git URL that `init --inherit` also makes absolute (see
the proposal), editing the user documentation.

## Decisions

### Decision: ADDED requirements only, no MODIFIED blocks

Every behavior is a new concern next to an existing requirement (`ADR
format recognized`, `Body seal recorded by the CLI`, `decision accept
accepts and seals…`, `codev init --inherit declares inherited sources`,
`codev docs --print prints the markdown source…`). Adding a requirement
leaves those blocks untouched, so archiving cannot lose detail from
them, and a reader still finds the line-ending rule in one place.

**Alternatives considered**: extending each existing requirement through
`## MODIFIED Requirements`. Rejected: five blocks copied in full for a
paragraph each, with a real risk of drift at archive time, and the CRLF
rule would be split across three requirements.

### Decision: Specify the seal as not normalizing line endings

The seal hashes the bytes on disk; the existing test's comment calls the
LF/CRLF difference "documented as a risk". The spec states it, with a
scenario where converting a sealed body's line endings yields
`decision_seal_mismatch`. This is consistent with the `decision accept`
requirement ("the recorded hash is the hash of the text the user
wrote") and with ADR 0001: the core hashes, the shell does not touch the
bytes.

**Alternatives considered**: specifying a normalized seal. Rejected for
this change: it is a behavior change (and a migration of every existing
seal), so it needs its own codev change.

### Decision: The forward-slash rule covers only paths codev makes absolute

`init` rewrites a relative path with `/`; a path given absolute or with
`~` is written as given, so `--inherit C:\shared` keeps its backslashes.
The requirement says so explicitly instead of promising forward slashes
for every `path:` value, which the code does not do.

**Alternatives considered**: a general "every inherited path uses `/`"
requirement. Rejected: false for absolute input today.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [The closed-pipe behavior has no automated test; the spec becomes its
  only guard] → Recorded here; a test (spawn `codev docs --print`, close
  the read end, assert exit 0 and empty stderr) belongs in a follow-up
  change, since this one touches no code. This contradicts the request's
  premise that tests already exist for all four behaviors.
- [The "another write failure" scenario of the closed-pipe requirement is
  hard to reproduce portably (e.g. `/dev/full` exists only on Linux)] →
  It describes the code path that already exists (`error:` on stderr,
  exit 1); a test, if added, can be Linux-only.
- [A Git checkout with `core.autocrlf` converts sealed ADR bodies and
  makes `validate` fail] → Now explicit in the spec; a fix
  (`.gitattributes` or a normalized seal) is a separate change.
- [The Windows scenario of `init` relies on the Windows CI job running
  the in-memory test with Unix-looking paths] → Acceptable: it is the
  coverage the code already has.

# Proposal: Specify behaviors that shipped without a spec

## Why

Four behaviors reached the code through ordinary pull requests, with their
tests, but no spec describes them: Windows (CRLF) line endings in ADRs,
warning callouts in the offline HTML docs, the silent exit when the reader
of `codev docs --print` closes the pipe, and forward slashes in the paths
`codev init --inherit` writes. Since `_codev/specs/` is authoritative, a
later change could remove any of them without breaking a requirement.

## What Changes

This change documents existing behavior only; no code changes.

- `decisions`: an ADR whose lines end in `\r\n` is parsed like one in
  `\n`; its seal hashes the body byte for byte, with no line-ending
  normalization; `codev decision accept` rewrites its frontmatter with
  `\r\n` and leaves the body untouched.
- `docs`: in the HTML, a blockquote that opens on a bold `Warning` or
  `Attention` title is rendered as a warning callout, styled apart from
  other blockquotes.
- `docs`: when stdout is closed before `codev docs --print` has finished
  writing (`codev docs --print | head`), the command exits 0 and prints
  no error.
- `init`: the absolute path `codev init --inherit` writes for a relative
  local path uses `/` as separator on every platform, Windows included.

Assumptions, made without being able to ask:

- "Slashes in inheritance paths" means the `path:` value `codev init
  --inherit` writes into `_codev/config.yaml`. The forward-slash JSON
  contract (`to_slash`) is not about inheritance and stays out of scope.
- The requirements describe the code as it is, including its limits: the
  seal is not normalized, so converting an ADR body between CRLF and LF
  changes its hash. That is what the code and its test
  (`hash_with_crlf_is_supported`) do; changing it would be a new change,
  not this one.
- Only the `**Warning**` and `**Attention**` titles are covered, the set
  the code and the website theme recognize.

Observed but out of scope: `codev init --inherit` also makes a relative
local *git* URL absolute (with forward slashes). No spec covers it and no
test exercises it; it is left for a separate change rather than specified
here without a test.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: ADRs saved with Windows line endings

An ADR whose lines end in `\r\n` (a file saved or checked out on
Windows) SHALL be read exactly like the same ADR with lines ending in
`\n`: same frontmatter fields, and a body that starts after the closing
`---` line and its own line ending.

The body seal MUST hash the body bytes as they are on disk, without
normalizing line endings: an ADR body converted from `\n` to `\r\n`, or
the reverse, after it was sealed no longer matches its seal.

When a command rewrites the `status` of a decision whose file starts
with `---\r\n` (`codev decision accept`, for the accepted decision and
for each decision it supersedes), the rewritten frontmatter MUST use
`\r\n` line endings, and the body MUST stay byte for byte identical, its
`\r\n` line endings included.

#### Scenario: A CRLF ADR is parsed like an LF one

- **GIVEN** an ADR `0001` with `id`, `title`, `status: accepted` and
  `date`, whose every line ends in `\r\n`
- **WHEN** codev reads the decisions (`codev decision list`,
  `codev validate`)
- **THEN** `0001` is listed with the same identifier, title and status
  as the same file with `\n` line endings
- **AND** no `decision_missing_frontmatter` finding is reported for it

#### Scenario: Accepting a CRLF decision keeps its line endings

- **GIVEN** a local ADR `0002` with `status: proposed`, whose every line
  ends in `\r\n`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev decision accept 0002`
- **THEN** the frontmatter of `0002` carries `status: accepted` followed
  by `\r\n`
- **AND** no line of the file mixes `\n` and `\r\n` endings
- **AND** the body of `0002` is byte for byte identical to the body
  before the command
- **AND** `codev validate` reports no `decision_seal_mismatch` for `0002`

#### Scenario: Converting the line endings of a sealed body breaks the seal

- **GIVEN** a sealed ADR `0003` whose body uses `\n` line endings
- **AND** its body is then rewritten with `\r\n` line endings, without
  any other edit
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev validate`
- **THEN** a `decision_seal_mismatch` error names `0003`

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Warning callouts stand out in the HTML documentation

In the HTML that `codev docs` generates (opened by default or written
with `--write`), a blockquote whose first paragraph opens on the bold
title `Warning` (`> **Warning**`) or `Attention` (`> **Attention**`, its
French equivalent) SHALL be rendered as a warning callout: marked with
the class `warning`, and styled by the inline stylesheet with its own
background, rule color and title color, in both the light and the dark
color scheme. Any other blockquote, including one that opens on another
bold title such as `**Note**`, MUST stay a plain blockquote.

`codev docs --print` is not affected: it prints the markdown source
unchanged.

#### Scenario: Warning and Attention become callouts

- **GIVEN** documentation containing a blockquote opening on
  `**Warning**` and another opening on `**Attention**`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev docs --write out.html`
- **THEN** both blockquotes carry `class="warning"` in `out.html`
- **AND** `out.html` styles `blockquote.warning` inline, with no
  external request

#### Scenario: A note stays a plain blockquote

- **GIVEN** documentation containing a blockquote opening on `**Note**`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev docs --write out.html`
- **THEN** that blockquote is rendered without the `warning` class

### Requirement: `codev docs --print` exits quietly when its reader leaves

When the standard output of `codev docs --print` is closed before the
whole documentation has been written — its reader exited, as in
`codev docs --print | head` — the command SHALL stop writing, print
nothing on stderr, and exit with code 0. Any other write failure on
stdout MUST still print an `error:` line on stderr and exit with
code 1.

#### Scenario: Piping into `head`

- **GIVEN** the current binary
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev docs --print | head -n 5`
- **THEN** the first five lines of the documentation are shown
- **AND** `codev` prints nothing on stderr
- **AND** the exit code of `codev` is 0

#### Scenario: Another write failure is reported

- **GIVEN** a standard output that rejects writes for a reason other
  than a closed pipe (for example a full device)
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev docs --print`
- **THEN** stderr carries a line starting with `error:`
- **AND** the exit code is 1

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Inherited paths written by `codev init` use forward slashes

When `codev init --inherit` turns a relative local path into an absolute
one to write it under `inherits:`, the written `path:` value SHALL use
`/` as its only separator, on every platform — Windows included, where
the native separator is `\`. The value MUST be written without escaped
backslashes, so that `_codev/config.yaml` stays identical whatever
machine ran `codev init`, and MUST resolve to the given folder when the
other codev commands read it back.

A path given as absolute or starting with `~` is written as given.

#### Scenario: A relative path is written absolute with forward slashes

- **GIVEN** a new project at `/home/you/project` and an existing folder
  `/home/you/conventions`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev init --yes --inherit ../conventions`
  from `/home/you/project`
- **THEN** `_codev/config.yaml` declares `path: /home/you/conventions`
- **AND** `codev status` reads the file without error

#### Scenario: A relative path on Windows

- **GIVEN** a new project at `C:\Users\you\project` and an existing
  folder `C:\Users\you\conventions`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev init --yes --inherit ..\conventions`
  from `C:\Users\you\project`
- **THEN** `_codev/config.yaml` declares `path: C:/Users/you/conventions`
- **AND** the file contains no `\` in that value
- **AND** `codev sources list` resolves the source to that folder

#### Scenario: A path starting with `~` is kept as given

- **GIVEN** an existing folder `~/shared`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev init --yes --inherit ~/shared`
- **THEN** `_codev/config.yaml` declares `path: ~/shared`
